title: Euler's theorem: eulerian graphs are those with all even degrees
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph that is connected and has at least one edge. Then $G$ is eulerian — that is, it admits an Euler tour, a closed walk traversing each edge exactly once — if and only if every vertex of $G$ has even degree.
hypotheses_covered: edge set is nonempty (at least one edge)
replaced:
Thm 4.1: a nonempty connected graph is eulerian iff it has no odd-degree vertex.

A nonempty connected graph is eulerian if and only if it has no
vertices of odd degree.
